whatItDoes: Calculates the profit margin on a product or service. Enter revenue and cost to see gross profit, profit margin as a percentage, and markup — while clearly flagging loss-making scenarios. Handles negative margins and lets you see the relationship between price, cost, and profitability instantly.
whyItExists: Pricing decisions hinge on the margin, not just on the price. Seeing the margin as a percentage of revenue, plus the markup on cost, tells a seller whether a business is actually making money after expenses.
whoShouldUse: Store owners, freelancers and agencies managing pricing, product managers, e-commerce sellers, and anyone setting a sell price for a product or service.
useCases: Set sell prices for B2B or B2C products
Check the profitability of a project before committing to it
Compare margins across the product catalog to find weak sellers
See the markup implied by your chosen selling price
Determine the minimum price that keeps a product profitable
Re-price a catalog when supplier costs change
instructions: Enter the total revenue or selling price
Enter the total cost of the product or service
Read gross profit, profit margin, markup, and whether it is a loss or gain
Adjust the price or cost to hit a target margin
Use the margin percentage for revenue-based pricing decisions
examples: Revenue $1,200, cost $850 → $350 gross profit, 29.2% margin, 41.2% markup
Revenue $100, cost $40 → $60 profit, 60% margin and 150% markup — the same profit expressed two ways
bestPractices: Include all operating costs—materials, labor, shipping, fees—in the cost field
Re-check margin whenever prices or raw costs change
Use margin for pricing; use markup for cost-based pricing math
Distinguish gross margin from net margin by layering in operating expenses
Aim for a margin that covers overhead, not just product cost
commonMistakes: Confusing margin (profit as % of revenue) with markup (profit as % of cost)
Overlooking fees and overhead that belong in cost
Basing decisions on selling price alone without the margin check
Not updating costs as suppliers change prices
Treating a positive revenue as a profit without checking the margin
faq: What is the difference between margin and markup? — Margin is profit divided by revenue; markup is profit divided by cost.
Can the tool handle losses? — Yes, it flags a negative profit or loss clearly.
Is this good for a freelancer's rate? — Yes, enter the rate as revenue and your time cost as the cost.
Are the computations local? — Yes, nothing is transmitted.
What is a healthy profit margin? — It varies by industry; retail often runs 5-10% while SaaS and agencies target far higher.
Should I price on margin or markup? — Use margin to evaluate profitability relative to price, and markup when building a price from cost.
